    🟢 Tolumin¶

    "Every stone we cut together is a border erased."

    Tolumin is the faith of the Koebi Tribe — the tall, green-colored demon subrace of the southern Demon Continent whose culture fuses hard work and meditation. Tolumin teaches that the purpose of the bin is to unite the Demon Continent — not through conquest like the Kutra superpower dream, but through shared labor made sacred.

    It is a sect of Kirivs-bin that reads Kirivis as unifier rather than merely as revealer.

    Origins¶

    Tolumin emerged from Vash-ka — the Koebi meditative discipline in which physical labor and spiritual contemplation are one act. A Koebi stonecutter meditating through the cutting was already erasing the line between self and work; Tolumin erases the line between self and continent the same way.

    The faith's name comes from tolu-min — "light-through-stone" — the moment when a Koebi-carved meditation chamber, hewn from a single boulder, is thinned enough that dawn light passes through without breaking the walls.

    Around ~250 BGD, the Koebi monastery-council — the most accomplished Vash-ka practitioners, who lead by demonstration rather than election — declared that the highest practice of the bin is not individual perfection but continental coherence. Kirivis revealed that the Shadows divided Ge'or; to honor him is to mend division, beginning with the Demon Continent itself.

    Tolumin has no prophet, only exemplary stonecutters. Its "saints" are remembered as the builders of particular chambers, bridges, and terraces that still stand centuries later.

    Beliefs¶

    • Kirivis is the unifier — Tolumin's reading of the last great legend foregrounds what Asatru histories minimize: Kirivis did not only uncover the Hybrian conspiracy — he briefly united disparate demon tribes into a single war host to fight it. That unity, not just the revelation, is the lesson.
    • Work is the sacrament of unity — every act of labor performed meditatively and offered without territorial claim is a prayer for the continent. A Koebi stonecutter carving a meditation chamber for the Zakarutia snake-queen's palace (as once happened) was Toluist worship, not mere commission.
    • Meditation dissolves borders — Vash-ka extended to diplomacy: to meditate alongside someone of another tribe for a week is to make them a co-worker, and co-workers do not make borders.
    • The continent is one workshop — Tolumin envisions the Demon Continent as a single atelier with many benches: Asatru hammering policy, Malgardians binding lineage, Flames holding sky, Kutra planning flight, Yak hammering modestly. No bench is master.
    • Asceticism as shared surplus — bin simplicity becomes Toluist economics: surplus from efficient, meditative work is not hoarded but offered — as gifts, joint projects, and unclaimed infrastructure (roads, wells, meditation halls) that any traveler may use.

    Practices¶

    • Vash-ka labor — every task — farming, stonework, metalwork, diplomacy itself — is approached as meditation. There is no menial labor in Tolumin; all work is sacred.
    • Chamber carving — the signature practice: carving a meditation chamber from a single boulder until light passes through. The first light-through is celebrated as a minor festival; the chamber is then gifted or left open for any wayfarer.
    • Joint-work pilgrimage — Koebi bands travel to other demon nations to labor alongside their hosts for a season (building a terrace in Maomodor Kingdom, repairing a Blazeyard pass, helping Kutra shore a riverbank). The labor is the pilgrimage.
    • Meditation exchange — Koebi councils host long, silent sittings with delegations from other tribes — sometimes days without a word. Decisions made afterward are considered Toluist consensus even when no formal vote was taken.
    • Honor duel, Koebi form — a duel of endurance, not combat: two disputants perform the same difficult physical task (holding a stone overhead, carrying water without spilling) until one yields gracefully. To endure longer and still yield is highest honor.

    Relation to Kirivs-bin¶

    Tolumin is Kirivs-bin universalized.

    • Shares every tenet: legends are scripture, Kirivis is the last great legend, action is prayer, honor is earned, comfort is the enemy
    • Where plain Kirivs-bin is individual (each demon walks the way alone), Tolumin is continental — the way is walked together, as a single people
    • Where Farsightism wants a superpower built by statecraft, Tolumin wants unity built by shared work — the difference is often framed as Kutra planning unity vs. Koebi practicing it
    • No priesthood apart from the monastery-council; no temples apart from open meditation chambers — structurally the closest sect to plain Kirivs-bin, and therefore the least controversial among Asatru purists

    Asatru theologians call Tolumin "the bin at its most generous." Some Kutra strategists call it "the bin at its most naive" — and then invite Koebi mason-teams anyway.

    Influence¶

    • Majority: Koebi Tribe — universal; the monastery-council is both government and synod
    • Minority/admired: small Toluist circles in Maomodor Kingdom (which shares the multi-species "demonic nationality" instinct), Blazeyard passes, and Asatru craft guilds
    • Craft reputation: Koebi-crafted tools, weapons, and meditation chambers traded across the continent carry implicit Toluist witness — "we made this for you, not only for ourselves"
    • Diplomatic role: historically the most welcome demon mediators; the Zakarutia snake-queen's chamber commission became legend precisely because a green stonecutter-monk negotiated nothing and offered everything
